subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Transport in which small particles bounce along the river bed is called:
questions.explain: Saltation is the bouncing or hopping of small particles along the bed.

questions.q: The process by which water turns from liquid into vapour and rises into the atmosphere is:
questions.explain: Evaporation turns liquid water into water vapour that rises into the air.

questions.q: A delta forms where a river:
options: Deposits its load as it enters a sea or lake
Begins at its source on a mountain
questions.explain: Deltas form where a river deposits sediment as it slows on entering still water.

questions.q: The flat area either side of a river that floods and is built up by deposited sediment is the:
questions.explain: A floodplain is the wide, flat valley floor built up by sediment left behind when the river floods.

questions.q: Groynes are wooden or rock barriers built out into the sea in order to:
options: Trap sediment and build up the beach
questions.explain: Groynes interrupt longshore drift, trapping sediment to widen the beach.

questions.q: On the INSIDE of a meander bend, where the water is slower, the river usually:
options: Deposits sediment forming a slip-off slope (point bar)
questions.explain: Slower flow on the inner bend deposits sediment, building a gently sloping point bar.

questions.q: A disadvantage of using groynes as a coastal defence is that they:
options: Starve beaches further along the coast of sediment, increasing erosion there
questions.explain: By trapping sediment, groynes deprive beaches downdrift, which can erode more quickly.

questions.q: Mass movement at the coast, such as a landslide or slumping, occurs when:
options: Sediment is carried out to sea by waves
Material moves down a cliff under gravity, often after rain saturates it
questions.explain: Mass movement is the downhill movement of cliff material under gravity, often triggered by water saturation.

questions.q: The boundary separating one drainage basin from another is the:
questions.explain: The watershed is the ridge of high land marking the edge of a drainage basin.

questions.q: A wave-cut platform is formed as:
options: Sediment is deposited at a river mouth
A cliff retreats, leaving a rocky surface at its base
A stack collapses into a stump
questions.explain: As waves undercut and the cliff retreats, a flat rocky platform is left at the base.

questions.q: On a coast with alternating hard and soft rock, resistant rock tends to form ____ and softer rock forms ____.
questions.explain: Resistant rock juts out as headlands while softer rock is eroded back into bays.

questions.q: Natural raised banks of sediment along the edges of a river channel are called:
questions.explain: Levees are raised banks built up by repeated deposition during floods.

questions.q: A river generally has its greatest discharge and carries its largest total load in its:
questions.explain: By the lower course, tributaries have added water, so discharge and total load are greatest.

questions.q: When rocks knock together and become smaller and rounder, the process is:
questions.explain: Attrition wears rocks down as they collide, making them smaller and rounder.

questions.q: Beach nourishment is an example of:
questions.explain: Beach nourishment, adding sand or shingle, is a soft engineering approach.

questions.q: Vertical erosion in a river's upper course tends to create which valley shape?
questions.explain: In the upper course the river cuts down vertically, forming a steep V-shaped valley.

questions.q: On a flood hydrograph, the 'lag time' is the gap between:
questions.explain: Lag time is the delay between the heaviest rainfall and the river reaching its highest discharge.

questions.q: Constructive waves are best described as:
options: Waves that flow inland as rivers
High, frequent waves with a strong backwash that erode beaches
Low, gentle waves with a strong swash that build up beaches
Waves that only occur in storms
questions.explain: Constructive waves have a strong swash and weak backwash, depositing material to build beaches.

questions.q: When a spit grows across a bay, joining two headlands and trapping a lagoon behind it, it forms a:
questions.explain: A bar forms where a spit extends across a bay, often enclosing a lagoon.

questions.q: Which is an example of HARD engineering river flood management?
options: Allowing the river to flood washland
Building a concrete dam and reservoir
questions.explain: Dams and reservoirs are hard engineering structures that control river flow.

questions.q: A salt marsh often develops behind a spit because:
options: The sheltered water allows fine sediment and mud to be deposited
questions.explain: Sheltered, calm water behind a spit lets mud and silt settle, creating a salt marsh.

questions.q: On the outside of a meander bend, the river mainly:
options: Erodes, forming a steep river cliff
Deposits sediment forming a slip-off slope
questions.explain: Faster flow on the outer bend erodes the bank, creating a river cliff.
